answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: 1929–1945 · German-born diarist, murdered at Bergen-Belsen aged 15
answer.sourceLine: Wikiquote’s sourced entry ↗ attributes this passage to a short piece titled “Give!”, dated 26 March 1944, written while Anne Frank was in hiding in Amsterdam — and files it under Tales from the Secret Annex, not the diary. We are stopping short of calling it verified: every scanned edition of that collection is lending-restricted, so no primary text could be opened, and Wikiquote records this exact English wording only as a variant translation without naming its translator. The attribution to Anne Frank is not in doubt; the wording is what we could not confirm at the source.
answer.confidenceText: Attributed — the piece and date are documented, but no primary text was opened to confirm this English wording.

source.excerpt: How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before beginning to improve the world! […] You can always, always give something, even if it is only kindness!
trail: The piece and the date — Wikiquote’s Anne Frank entry ↗ attributes this passage to “Give!” (26 March 1944) and prints both English renderings, ours as the variant translation.

Not the diary — Wikiquote keeps The Diary of a Young Girl and Tales from the Secret Annex ↗ in separate sections, and files “Give!” under the latter. The short pieces were written into a separate journal begun on 2 September 1943 and recovered with her other manuscripts after her arrest.

The translations — library catalogue records show two English lineages for the collection: Ralph Manheim and Michel Mok ↗ and, for the revised 2003 edition, Susan Massotty ↗. We could not open either text — both are lending-restricted — so we do not say which produced this wording.
source.excerptNote: The passage as Wikiquote ↗ gives this translation. Its other rendering of the same lines reads “How wonderful it is that no one has to wait… You can always — always — give something, even if it’s a simple act of kindness!”

author.name: Anne Frank
author.heading: About Anne Frank
author.bio: Anne Frank spent twenty-five months hidden in an Amsterdam annex, where she wrote far more than the diary she is known for: short stories, essays, recollections and the opening chapters of a novel. She was fourteen when she wrote “Give!”. She was arrested that August and died at Bergen-Belsen the following year, and the manuscripts survived only because Miep Gies and Bep Voskuijl gathered them from the floor of the emptied hiding place.

misattribution.heading: Genuine — but not from the diary
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Anne Frank is sound. What is nearly always wrong is the book: this is not a diary entry, and the English wording is one of two competing translations rather than a fixed sentence.

items.scope: Where it is usually said to come from
items.why: “Give!” belongs to Tales from the Secret Annex ↗, the separate collection of stories and essays, which Wikiquote ↗ keeps in its own section away from the diary.

items.who: “even if it’s a simple act of kindness!”
items.why: The same Dutch sentence, rendered differently. Neither English form is “the” quotation — both are translations, and they differ in more than punctuation.

Wikiquote attributes the piece to her and dates it 26 March 1944, and Tales from the Secret Annex ↗ was recovered with the rest of her manuscripts from the annex. What is unconfirmed is the English wording, not the author.
Both English lineages of the collection — Manheim and Mok ↗ and Massotty ↗ — are lending-restricted on the Internet Archive, so neither text could be read. We do not know which produced this wording.

misattribution.truthLine: Hers, and dated — just not a diary entry, and not a wording we could confirm at the source. The piece is “Give!”, 26 March 1944, collected in Tales from the Secret Annex ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: She wrote it four months before the arrest, at fourteen, hidden in a building she could not leave. “Give!” is an argument, not a diary note — a short essay about what people owe each other, written by someone with almost nothing left to give.

The line that travels is the last one, but the piece around it is harder and better: it presses the reader on why the poor are tolerated at all, and insists nobody has to wait for permission to begin.
detailsBody: Alongside the diary, Anne kept a separate journal from 2 September 1943 for stories, essays and memories — some invented, some about life in the annex, some about her school days before it. “Give!” is one of the essays, and the collection also holds the first chapters of a novel she never finished.

All of it was left on the floor when the family was taken on 4 August 1944, and gathered up by Miep Gies and Bep Voskuijl. The stories were first published in the Netherlands in 1949, expanded in 1960, and issued complete in 1982.
context.pull: Written at fourteen, in hiding, four months before the arrest.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote attributes "You can always, always give something, even if it is only kindness!" to Anne Frank’s "Give!" (26 March 1944), as a variant translation, and files "Give!" under Tales from the Secret Annex rather than the diary.

Tales from the Secret Annex is a separate collection from the diary, written into a journal begun 2 September 1943, first published in the Netherlands in 1949, expanded in 1960 and issued complete in 1982; the manuscripts were recovered by Miep Gies and Bep Voskuijl after the arrest of 4 August 1944.
An English edition of Anne Frank’s Tales from the Secret Annex was translated by Ralph Manheim and Michel Mok.
The revised 2003 Bantam edition of the Tales credits Susan Massotty as translator.
Anne Frank was a German-born Jewish diarist who hid in Amsterdam from 1942 until the family’s arrest in 1944.
